beats.title: What a tax is
beats.narration: A tax is a compulsory payment to a government used to fund public services like roads, schools, defence, and administration. Taxes can be on income, consumption, property, or wealth.

citations.quote: A tax is a compulsory contribution that funds shared public services.
citations.full_passage_text: Governments levy taxes to raise revenue and, sometimes, to influence behaviour. Common bases include income, spending (sales/VAT/GST), property, and capital gains; the exact system differs by jurisdiction.

beats.title: Income tax and brackets
beats.narration: Many income taxes are progressive and use brackets: higher slices of income are taxed at higher rates. Your marginal rate applies to the last rupee earned; your effective rate is the average across all income.

citations.quote: A higher bracket taxes only the income within that bracket — not all of it.
citations.full_passage_text: In a bracketed system, moving into a higher bracket does not tax your whole income at the higher rate — only the portion inside that bracket. That is why the marginal rate (on the last unit) is higher than the effective (average) rate.

beats.title: Deductions vs credits
beats.narration: A deduction reduces the income that is taxed; a credit reduces the tax itself. A credit of a given amount is usually worth more than a deduction of the same amount.

citations.quote: Deductions shrink taxable income; credits shrink the tax you owe.
citations.full_passage_text: Because a deduction only removes income before the rate is applied, its value depends on your rate. A credit subtracts directly from tax owed, so a $100 credit typically saves more than a $100 deduction.

beats.title: Capital gains basics
beats.narration: A capital gain is the profit from selling an asset for more than you paid. Many systems tax short-term and long-term gains differently, and some offer exemptions or indexation.

citations.quote: A capital gain is the profit when you sell an asset for more than its cost.
citations.full_passage_text: Gains are usually taxed when 'realised' (on sale), not while unrealised. Holding periods, asset types, and local rules (rates, exemptions, indexation, carry-forward of losses) vary widely — check your jurisdiction.

beats.title: Filing and records
beats.narration: Most taxpayers file a periodic return summarising income, deductions, and tax paid. Keeping organised records and meeting deadlines helps avoid penalties.

citations.quote: Keep records and meet deadlines — it prevents most avoidable penalties.
citations.full_passage_text: A tax return reconciles what you owe with what you've already paid (through withholding or advance tax). Good record-keeping, correct forms, and on-time filing reduce errors and penalties; when unsure, get professional help.
